title: 1. Introduction to HPC
content: A combination of techniques employed to optimize and take advantage of modern computer hardware. We use **FLOPS** (Floating-point Operations per Second). ## Supercomputer Architectures **Clusters**: A bunch of desktops linked together by a network. **Multi-core machines**: A collection of processors that can see and use the same memory. Limited number of cores and much more expensive when the machine is large. - *Accelerator machines*, are machines that contain an "off-host" accelerator that is used for computation. Most supercomputers are a hybrid of these kinds of architectures. ### Clusters Each processor is independent when data some other processor is needed, the other processor must send it. - Communication is hand-coded from program to program. ### Shared Memory Different processors acting on one large bank of memory were all processors see the same data. - All coordination and communication is done through this shared memory. - Each core is assigned a thread of execution of a single program that acts on the data. ### Hybrid Architectures Multicore nodes linked together with a high-speed interconnect. - The cores have vector capabilities #### Hybrid Accelerator Architecture Nodes also contain one or more accelerators. These are specialized, super-threaded (500 - 2000+) processors. - CUDA is used to program these devices
